ui_bugs.issue: RED-SCREEN CRASH on OTP step. As soon as user taps Send OTP and the app renders the 6 OTP TextInput boxes, react-dom throws `TypeError: Failed to set an indexed property [0] on 'CSSStyleDeclaration': Indexed property setter is not supported.` in setValueForStyle. Root cause: globalFont.ts patches TextInput.render via `React.cloneElement(el, { style: [{ fontFamily }, style] })`. When the original `style` is already an array (or when RN-Web passes it into the DOM style prop before flattening), react-dom receives an array style and tries to set numeric indices on the element's CSSStyleDeclaration. Reference: /app/frontend/src/lib/globalFont.ts:59-61. Blocks: brand-new phone registration for BOTH partner and merchant (all cascade tests). Repro: open app → skip onboarding → enter any new 10-digit phone → Send OTP → red screen.

Public Sans font is registered with document.fonts (MaterialDesignIcons, PublicSans-Regular/Medium/SemiBold/Bold/ExtraBold all present) but NOT applied to any Text element on web preview. Computed font-family on 'Welcome to AzoApp', 'MOBILE NUMBER', '+91', 'Send OTP', 'Register as Partner', 'Merchant Demo' etc. is all `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif` (system default). Only MDI icon glyphs get MaterialDesignIcons family. The patch appears applied to TextInput (evidence: it crashes it), but has no visible effect on Text on RN-Web. Reference: /app/frontend/src/lib/globalFont.ts (whole module). The feature 'app-wide Public Sans to match web' is functionally not achieved on web preview.

react_native_issues.issue: Runtime patch of Text.render and TextInput.render via `Comp.render = function(...){ ... React.cloneElement(el, { style: [{ fontFamily }, style] }) }` is incompatible with react-native-web. On web, TextInput's inner element receives the resulting style array and passes it to react-dom which cannot iterate an array as a CSSStyleDeclaration. Recommended fixes (main agent to choose): (a) flatten before returning: `style: StyleSheet.flatten([{ fontFamily }, style])` so the final prop is a single object; (b) on web, drop the runtime render patch entirely and inject a CSS rule (e.g. `* { font-family: 'PublicSans-Regular', ... }` in a `<style>` tag via useEffect + Platform.OS==='web') because the patch also does NOT actually change computed font-family on web anyway; (c) use `Text.defaultProps.style` merge (RN legacy) or a Theme provider that supplies fontFamily to typography tokens. Reference: /app/frontend/src/lib/globalFont.ts:45-63. Also note: on native (Expo Go/iOS/Android) the same array-style form is fine, but the DOM issue is specific to react-native-web.

critical_code_review_comments: globalFont.ts's runtime monkey-patch of forwardRef.render on Text/TextInput is fragile: it mutates a shared React internal, is not tree-shakeable, and breaks under RN-Web's style pipeline. Prefer a Platform.OS-gated CSS injection for web and (on native) use `Text.defaultProps` + StyleSheet.compose. Also, `installGlobalFont` is guarded with a module-level `patched` flag but is called from `RootLayout()` body directly on every render (`if (fontsLoaded) installGlobalFont();`) — safe due to idempotency, but move into a `useEffect` for clarity.

app/_layout.tsx line 97 `if (fontsLoaded) installGlobalFont();` runs during render — technically fine because of the `patched` guard, but preferred pattern is `useEffect(() => { if (fontsLoaded) installGlobalFont(); }, [fontsLoaded]);` to make side-effects explicit.

rca_of_issue: PRIMARY BUG — OTP screen red-screen crash. Repro: (1) open https://merchant-panel-sync.preview.emergentagent.com; (2) dismiss onboarding; (3) enter any new 10-digit mobile; (4) tap Send OTP → screen navigates to OTP step and immediately renders ErrorBoundary with message `Failed to set an indexed property [0] on 'CSSStyleDeclaration': Indexed property setter is not supported.` — stack: `at setValueForStyle (react-dom)`. Cause: globalFont.ts:52-62 patches `TextInput.render` and returns `React.cloneElement(el, { style: [{ fontFamily }, style] })`. When TextInput's internal render tree passes this array to a DOM node (react-native-web's input path in some flows), react-dom's `setValueForStyle` treats the array as a CSSStyleDeclaration object and tries `style['0'] = ...` which browsers reject. Login's single phone TextInput is small/simple and doesn't hit the same code path, but the OTP screen's 6 stacked TextInputs (or the KeyboardAwareScrollView interaction) does. Mitigation options for main agent: (A) flatten style — `React.cloneElement(el, { style: StyleSheet.flatten([{ fontFamily }, style]) })`; (B) skip the runtime patch entirely on Platform.OS === 'web' and inject a global CSS rule via a `<style>` tag; (C) revert the globalFont module and rely on a per-component fontFamily via theme tokens. Recommend (A)+(B): flatten on native, CSS on web. SECONDARY BUG — Public Sans not visually applied on web preview even though fonts are loaded. `document.fonts.check('16px PublicSans-Regular')` returns false and computed font-family stays system default on every non-icon Text. The runtime render-patch approach doesn't influence react-native-web's generated inline-style/class-based typography path.
